title: Shaping the spread: Influence of distributor vane design on fertilizer distribution uniformity
content:
by Fırat Kömekçi, Erkan Urkan, Ceren Kömekçi, Hüseyin Güler, Erdem Aykas

Achieving uniform fertilizer distribution with disc-type spreaders is critical for both crop nutrition and environmental sustainability, yet it remains challenging due to the numerous influencing parameters. This study specifically investigates the impact of distributor vane geometry on the coefficient of variation (CV, %) of twin-disc broadcasters. Four custom-designed vane configurations named hollow-channel, double-channel, quad-channel, and inclined-channel were developed and manufactured. Controlled bench tests were conducted using compound fertilizer in strict accordance with the ASAE S341.4 standard, with all trials performed in triplicate to ensure statistical reliability. The results revealed a clear trade-off between distribution precision and effective working width. The quad-channel vane delivered the highest distribution uniformity, achieving a CV of 10.12%, although its effective working width was limited to 14.64 meters. In contrast, the hollow-channel vane provided acceptable uniformity (CV of 14.87%) while enabling a substantially wider effective working width of 14.64 m, offering greater field efficiency through reduced pass-to-pass overlap. Statistical analysis confirmed that the vane geometry had a significant effect on the CV (p < 0.05). The superior performance of the quad-channel design is attributed to its ability to better balance the radial and tangential velocity components of granular particles at the point of disc release, thereby minimizing erratic collisions and stabilizing the lateral spread pattern. These findings provide actionable guidance for both manufacturers and end-users: the quad-channel vane is recommended for precision agriculture where application accuracy is paramount, whereas the hollow-channel vane serves as a practical, high-capacity alternative for large-scale operations where maximizing working width and minimizing fuel consumption take priority. This study underscores that optimizing vane geometry is a highly effective, low-cost strategy for improving field-scale fertilizer efficiency.
